### Advisory

- Unvalidated free-text marker fields are interpolated verbatim into model-visible output: describe() relays marker['outdated_reason']/['written_at']/['claimed_at'] into the resume listing and start notice (additionalContext/systemMessage), and injection_context() relays outdated_reason into the injected handover context. marker_problem validates names/paths but not these strings, so a planted outdated-*/claimed-* marker (same-user writable .claude/rotation) can place arbitrary text in the model's context even though the diff declares these files untrusted inputs. Same-user boundary, not privilege escalation, but worth sanitizing/bounding. (severity: warning)
- int(words[0]) raises ValueError for a purely numeric index longer than Python's 4300-digit int-conversion limit, so a mistyped /context-rotation:rotate resume argument turns into a hook failure (exit 1, 'list handovers failed: ValueError'). The isascii()/isdigit() guard signals intent to tolerate arbitrary input; cap the length or catch ValueError and return the 'with a number from the list' message. (severity: info)
- read_regular() reads untrusted rotation files with an unbounded handle.read(); a planted huge ready-*.json or a handover named by a marker is fully loaded into memory on every scan/hook, so the 'opened without blocking' guarantee does not cover size. A sane size cap (markers are tiny; handovers are bounded by handover_max_chars at write time) would keep a same-user memory DoS out of the hot path. (severity: info)
- test_registered_events_and_their_entries assigns registered[event] = ... per hook group, so if an event ever gains a second group (e.g. a matcher-scoped additional hook) the test silently records only the last one instead of failing. Assert on a list/set of groups per event. (severity: info)
- CHANGELOG entry is a run-on: '(B2, C) The files under ...' is missing a sentence break/period after '(B2, C)', making two unrelated statements one sentence in an otherwise carefully punctuated changelog. (severity: info)
